notes: The whole image is 1670×2143 pixels; the supplied upper half is 1670×1151 and lower half 1670×1152. All boxes in this report use whole-image coordinates.

Title: “Résumé de quelques résultats de Kostant (sous groupes simples de rang 1).” The page states a theorem with conditions a), b), cancelled b′), c), c′), d), followed by consequences and a part (ii) on nilpotent elements and conjugacy.

The handwritten reference contains “Oct.1959”; this is bibliographical information, not a stated composition date. The lower-left archive annotation reads 15. No separate printed author page number is visible.
The theorem introduction leaves a physical blank after “propre de”. No ad(x), x, or illegibility placeholder is substituted for that unprinted interval.

The live b) line prints g(0)→g(-2), and part (ii) prints “lorsque e=0” beside u≠1. Both surprising readings are preserved. The independent slash in the following i.e. is represented at its actual position.

No explicit verbal hesitation or question is written here. The deletion of b′) and the overstruck conjugacy wording are documentary revisions; the doubt marks in reading.tex are the reader’s, not source question marks.
The b) handwritten addition says “pour f”. Its first subscript, group-parameter prime, and partly cancelled neighboring line remain locally uncertain.
Raised typed “par” and handwritten “Z=” have no caret fixing one common insertion point. The text layout preserves their staggered positions above the cancelled phrase.

Agreement loci were read as well as disputes, including the full title, both theorem paragraphs, the formulas in a), c), c′), the basis description, all surviving words in (ii), and the unfinished final “ou encore les”. The continuation was not supplied.
No diagrams or mathematical pictures occur. The small nonverbal slash is preserved by TikZ; connector strokes and underlines are represented through the corresponding insertion/underline states.

math_checks.check: Assuming [x,e]=2e and [x,v]=jv, Jacobi gives [x,[e,v]]=[[x,e],v]+[e,[x,v]]=(j+2)[e,v]. Thus ad(e) raises x-weight by 2, and its k-th power sends weight -k to weight k.
math_checks.result: The endpoints in a) are consistent with this calculation. The printed b) target -2 is not the weight obtained from a weight-0 input, which prompted an ink check; the clearly visible minus is retained. This does not prove or disprove the page’s full equivalence theorem.

math_checks.result: The juxtaposition e=0 and u≠1 is inconsistent under the page’s definition u=exp(e). The equality has no crossing stroke, so no correction was made.
